findings.rationale: SC's observed outcome prevalence is far above what its features imply, with normal discrimination. Pooled round-20 local metrics show CITL of -0.35, prevalence 0.59 against mean predicted risk 0.24, and AUC 0.805 (normal). Subgroup O/E is about 2.5 in both sexes, so the excess is client-wide rather than subgroup-specific. The CITL is already negative in round 1 (-0.26, prevalence 0.78) and stays negative in most rounds, so the shift dates from the start. Its updates are also anomalous: the median norm is about 5.8x the median client, the mean cosine is negative, and the norm grows over rounds. These are consistent with a persistent prevalence mismatch. Local performance is abnormal, so this is not classed as poisoning.

CA's observed prevalence is far above its predicted risk, with normal AUC. Round-20 CITL is -0.35 with prevalence 0.55 against mean predicted 0.20, and AUC is 0.836. Subgroup O/E is about 2.6 to 2.9 in both sexes. The CITL is negative in every round from round 1 (-0.27), so the mismatch is present from the start. The update norm is about 4.6x the median and the mean cosine is negative, with the norm growing over rounds. Local performance is abnormal, so the anomalous updates are explained by the data rather than by poisoning. The drift tool's onset of round 8 rests on noisy feature-shift values and is not treated as independent evidence.

VT's observed prevalence is about 0.49 against a mean predicted risk of 0.17 at round 20, giving a CITL of -0.32 (z about -15). AUC is normal at 0.818. Subgroup O/E is about 3.3 and 2.3 in the two sex groups, which points to a client-wide prevalence excess. Its updates are moderately anomalous (median norm about 2.5x, mean cosine -0.21). Per-round drift values for VT are very noisy, so the onset of round 1 is a low-confidence estimate rather than a measured change point.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then drilled into the suspicious clients. Three clients (SC, CA, VT) show the same pattern: observed outcome prevalence far above what their features imply (CITL about -0.32 to -0.35, observed prevalence about 0.49 to 0.59 against predicted 0.17 to 0.24), with normal AUC and subgroup O/E about 2.3 to 3.3 in both sexes. That matches prevalence_shift rather than label_noise (which would lower AUC) or subgroup_bias (which would show O/E below 1 in one group). SC and CA show it from round 1 and also have anomalous updates (norm 4.6x to 5.8x the median, negative mean cosine). Those updates are explained by the prevalence mismatch rather than poisoning, since local performance is abnormal. VT's evidence is somewhat weaker and its onset is uncertain. Other flags (drift on CA, SC, LA, VI, MI; feature outliers such as DC/NC/VT HighBP and SD HighChol; subgroup leads MS/WV income 4, FL age group 9) all had |z_noise| below about 4.5 and were not corroborated by a second tool, so I did not report them. No evidence of poisoning, free-riding, explanation instability, missing-value sentinels or subgroup under-diagnosis was found. The full 20 epsilon was spent, so the three findings rest on the screening-level evidence above.
